S01.label: dresser tipover
S01.why: Plain keyword needs the literal token 'tipover' and returns 0 hits; stemming + synonyms (tipover -> tip over, dresser -> chest of drawers) put South Shore's 'Chest of Drawers ... Tip-Over' recall at #1 and all 10 AFTER results are dresser/clothing-storage tip-over recalls.

S01.label: ebike battery fire
S01.why: No notice contains the token 'ebike', so plain keyword returns 0 hits; the synonym map expands ebike -> e bike / electric bicycle and AFTER's top 7 are all e-bike fire recalls (VIVI, Ancheer, Gyroor, Santa Cruz x2, Pacific Cycle, FENGQS).

S01.label: CO alarm failed to alert
S01.hint: CO alarms that fail to alert
S01.why: Notices say 'carbon monoxide' and 'failure to alert', so all-terms plain keyword returns 0 hits; CO -> carbon monoxide plus stemming puts New Cosmos' natural gas/CO alarms at #1 and the CHZHVAN smoke/CO detectors at #3.

S01.label: li-ion power banks overheating
S01.why: Plain keyword requires the literal 'li-ion' and 'overheating' and returns 0 hits; li ion -> lithium ion and stemming put Fantasia/Anker, ESR HaloLock and Anker power-bank recalls at #1-3 (7 of the top 10 are power banks).

S02.label: baby fell asleep in the angled rocker and stopped breathing
S02.query: baby fell asleep in the angled rocker and stopped breathing
S02.why: BM25 latches onto 'baby' (Cpzzkq loungers, 4moms strap-entanglement rockers, baby walkers) with no inclined-sleep recall in its top 3; vector reads 'angled rocker ... stopped breathing' as inclined sleep and returns Fisher-Price Rock 'n Play, Kids II Rocking Sleepers and Kolcraft's inclined sleeper at #1-3.

S02.label: my phone's portable charger got hot and melted in my bag
S02.query: my phone's portable charger got hot and melted in my bag
S02.why: BM25 matches 'portable' and 'hot' (water immersion heaters, infant swings, jewelry kits) and first reaches a battery phone case at #5; vector maps 'portable charger' to power banks and returns myCharge, Belkin and Daniel M. Friedman power-bank recalls at #1-3.

S02.label: my teenager's VR goggles padding gave her a rash on her face
S02.query: my teenager's VR goggles padding gave her a rash on her face
S02.why: No notice says 'VR goggles', 'padding' or 'rash', so BM25 returns unrelated infant-swing and burn-pad notices with nothing relevant in its top 10; vector puts the Oculus Quest 2 removable foam facial-interface (skin irritation) recall at #1.

S02.label: the paddles on the overhead fan in our living room came loose and fell
S02.query: the paddles on the overhead fan in our living room came loose and fell
S02.why: BM25 latches onto 'paddles' and 'fan' (Vornado tower heaters, stand-up paddleboard paddles) and only reaches the ceiling fan at #6; vector reads 'paddles on the overhead fan' as ceiling-fan blades and ranks the Hampton Bay Halwin ceiling fan recall #1.

S03.label: model EFMIS121 mini fridge sparking
S03.why: Keyword is pulled by 'mini' (Yoto Mini speakers, mini trampolines) and has the EFMIS121 notice only at #5; vector-only ranks the July-2025 Curtis minifridge recall (models EFMIS129-175, not EFMIS121) #1 and the expansion #2; hybrid puts the Jan-2026 expansion that adds model EFMIS121 at #1.

S03.label: SKU 34785 ice chest pinched finger
S03.why: Keyword latches onto 'chest' and 'finger' (Generac finger-amputation generators, chests of drawers) and has the Igloo expansion at #9; vector-only ranks the original Igloo 90-qt cooler recall (its SKU list lacks 34785) #1 and the expansion #2; hybrid puts the expansion that lists SKU 34785 at #1.

S03.label: model M0934E baby bed fall risk
S03.query: model M0934E baby bed fall risk
S03.why: Keyword matches 'bed' and 'fall' (Agrish adult bed rails, baby walkers, Murphy beds) and has the DaVinci notice at #5; vector-only ranks DaVinci's Dec-2019 bassinet recall (M0934G/Q/N/W, no M0934E) #1 and the July-2020 recall that lists M0934E #3; hybrid ranks the M0934E recall #1.

S03.label: TF30 jogging machine caught fire at the gym
S03.query: TF30 jogging machine caught fire at the gym
S03.why: Keyword grabs 'machine' and 'gym' (Sensio and SOWTECH espresso machines, Skip Hop activity gyms) and has the TF30 notice at #4; vector-only ranks the 2022 Matrix T1/T3 commercial treadmill recall (no TF30) #1 and the 2026 expansion #2; hybrid puts the expansion that adds the TF30 at #1.

S04.label: Which space heater could switch on by itself without anyone touching it?
S04.hint: Heater that turns on by itself
S04.query: Which space heater could switch on by itself without anyone touching it?
S04.why: Hybrid ranks generic space-heater fire recalls first (DREO, Shop LC, AmazonBasics) and Atomi at #4; the semantic reranker reads Atomi's hazard 'smart heaters can turn on without user input' and moves it to #1.

S04.label: Which recall involved honeycomb window shades from a well-known brand?
S04.query: Which recall involved honeycomb window shades from a well-known brand?
S04.why: Hybrid ranks Amazon roller-shade recalls (Shadeks, ChrisDowa) above Levolor at #3; the reranker connects 'honeycomb' with Levolor's 'Custom Cellular Shades' and moves it to #1.

S04.label: Which pretend-food play set had magnets a child could swallow?
S04.query: Which pretend-food play set had magnets a child could swallow?
S04.why: Hybrid fills its top 5 with generic magnet-set recalls (Mag Cube, magnetic building sticks, ball sets, chess games) and has Gagaku's Children's Ice Cream Toy Playsets at #6; the reranker recognizes 'pretend-food play set' and moves it to #1.

S04.label: Which children's dresser was sold exclusively at a furniture store chain and violated the new tip-over standard?
S04.query: Which children's dresser was sold exclusively at a furniture store chain and violated the new tip-over standard?
S04.why: Hybrid ranks the Winston Porter/Seeday and EnHomee dressers first and the Rooms To Go children's dressers at #3; the reranker matches 'children's dresser', 'sold exclusively at a furniture store chain' and the clothing-storage-unit regulation and moves it to #1.

S05.label: space heaters sold at Amazon with a refund
S05.hint: Space heaters on Amazon with refund
S05.query: space heaters sold at Amazon with a refund
S05.filter: category eq 'Heating & cooling' and retailers/any(r: r eq 'Amazon') and remedies/any(m: m eq 'refund')
S05.why: Keyword-only #2 is the DREO space heater (Home Depot/Lowe's/Costco/Best Buy, replacement remedy - ineligible) and #5 a water immersion heater; filters category=Heating & cooling, retailers=Amazon, remedies=refund leave 9 recalls with AmazonBasics, Shop LC and Vornado SRTH heaters at #1-3, and facets show all 9 fire-burn, refund, made in China.

S05.label: power banks under $75 sold on Amazon with burn injuries reported
S05.hint: Amazon power banks under $75 with injuries
S05.query: power banks under $75 sold on Amazon with burn injuries reported
S05.filter: category eq 'Batteries & chargers' and retailers/any(r: r eq 'Amazon') and priceMaxUsd le 75 and injuriesReported eq true
S05.why: Keyword #1 is the ESR HaloLock power bank recall ('No injuries have been reported') - ineligible; filters Batteries & chargers + Amazon + priceMaxUsd <= 75 + injuriesReported leave exactly the Anker ($60), Baseus ($55) and Fantasia/Anker ($70) power-bank recalls with reported burn injuries.

S05.label: children's products sold on Temu or Shein that violate federal safety rules
S05.query: children's products sold on Temu or Shein that violate federal safety rules
S05.filter: retailers/any(r: r eq 'Temu' or r eq 'Shein')
S05.why: Keyword #2 is Grizzly's children's tool kits sold on Amazon, not Temu or Shein; the retailer filter (Temu or Shein) returns SHEIN children's sleepwear and pajama sets and Temu-exclusive kids' bike helmets at #1-3, with category/retailer/hazard/remedy facets for the marketplace review.

S05.label: e-bikes, scooters and hoverboards sold on Amazon with injuries reported
S05.query: e-bikes, scooters and hoverboards sold on Amazon with injuries reported
S05.filter: category eq 'E-bikes & e-scooters' and retailers/any(r: r eq 'Amazon') and injuriesReported eq true
S05.why: Keyword's top 3 (VIVI e-bikes, Jetson hoverboards, FENGQS e-bikes) each fail a constraint - no injuries reported or sold only at Target; filters leave exactly Ancheer and Gyroor e-bikes and the Hover-1 Helix hoverboard, all sold on Amazon with burn or smoke-inhalation injuries.

S06.label: latest adult portable bed rail entrapment recall
S06.query: latest adult portable bed rail entrapment recall
S06.why: Hybrid ranks Medline (2024), Essential Medical's 2024 reannouncement and Agrish's original Jan-2026 notice first and the Oct-2026 'Agrish Reannounces and Expands' notice at #6; freshness puts that latest reannouncement at #1.

S06.label: latest fabric dresser tip-over recall
S06.why: Hybrid ranks the WLIVE fabric dressers (Oct 2025) and the original May-2026 Mainstays notice first; freshness lifts Walmart's Aug-2026 reannouncement of the Mainstays fabric dresser recall from #4 to #1 (the later Yuyitop and Winston Porter dressers are wood).

S06.label: largest pressure cooker burn hazard recall
S06.query: largest pressure cooker burn hazard recall
S06.why: Hybrid ranks Sensio (860,000 units), Ambiano (46,660) and Insignia (930,000) pressure cookers first; the units-recalled impact profile lifts SharkNinja's 1.8-million-unit Foodi pressure cooker recall from #4 to #1.

S06.label: biggest magnetic ball set ingestion recall
S06.query: biggest magnetic ball set ingestion recall
S06.why: Hybrid ranks small magnetic ball-set recalls first (Mag Cube 600 units, Joybuy sets 650 and 4,240); the units-recalled impact profile lifts the Zen Magnets/Neoballs recall (about 10 million units) from #6 to #1.

S07.label: Which products were recalled for violating Reese's Law on button batteries, and which dressers were recalled for violating the STURDY Act tip-over standard?
S07.query: Which products were recalled for violating Reese's Law on button batteries, and which dressers were recalled for violating the STURDY Act tip-over standard?
S07.why: Hybrid's top 9 are all STURDY-Act dresser recalls, leaving the Reese's Law half unanswered in its top 3; agentic retrieval returns SIG SAUER's Reese's Law violation #1, a STURDY dresser #2 and Pella's Reese's Law patio doors #3.

S07.label: Which roller window shades violated the federal window covering standard, and which aerosol bug spray cans could burst and cut people?
S07.hint: Window covering rule + bursting aerosol cans
S07.query: Which roller window shades violated the federal window covering standard, and which aerosol bug spray cans could burst and cut people?
S07.why: Hybrid's top 8 are roller-shade and roll-up blind recalls and the aerosol-can recall is only #9; agentic retrieval returns Maggie's Farm aerosol bed bug & flea killer cans #1 and LINKCOO and Shadeks roller shades #2-3.

S07.label: Which e-bikes were recalled for lithium-ion battery fires, and which kids' outfit had plastic cord tips that could pop off and choke a toddler?
S07.query: Which e-bikes were recalled for lithium-ion battery fires, and which kids' outfit had plastic cord tips that could pop off and choke a toddler?
S07.why: Hybrid's top 6 are all e-bike fire recalls and the TJX pants-set recall is absent from its top 10; agentic retrieval puts TJX's twill pants sets (plastic tips on the faux drawstrings can come off - choking) #1 and Ancheer e-bikes #2.

S07.label: Which power banks were recalled because the lithium-ion battery overheats, and which camping tents were falsely labeled as fire retardant?
S07.query: Which power banks were recalled because the lithium-ion battery overheats, and which camping tents were falsely labeled as fire retardant?
S07.why: Hybrid's top 5 are power-bank recalls and the Thermo Tents notice sits at #6; agentic retrieval returns Anker and Baseus power banks #1-2 and the Thermo Tents 'mislabeled as fire retardant' recall #3.

industries.label: Financial services
industries.blurb: OCC Comptroller’s Handbook, FDIC examination manual, interagency guidance and CFPB consumer complaints (company names masked).

sources.name: Consumer Complaint Database narratives
sources.license: Public domain (U.S. Government data); published narratives with company names masked

S01.label: KYC requirements for high risk customers
S01.query: KYC requirements for high risk customers
S01.why: Regulators never write 'KYC' (the FDIC BSA manual says customer due diligence/CDD), so all-terms plain keyword returns 0 hits; the synonym map expands KYC → customer due diligence/CDD and AFTER's #1–2 are the FDIC 8.1 'Customer Due Diligence (CDD)' and 'CDD Program Guidance' sections.

S01.label: EDD for private banking accounts
S01.why: 'EDD' never appears in regulator text (the corpus only uses it for California EDD unemployment cards), so plain keyword returns 0 hits; the synonym edd → enhanced due diligence puts the FDIC 8.1 'Enhanced Due Diligence for Non-U.S. Persons Maintaining Private Banking Accounts' sections at ranks 1–5.

S01.label: ISDA master agreement netting and collateral
S01.query: ISDA master agreement netting and collateral
S01.why: All-terms plain keyword needs 'ISDA' in the same chunk as master/agreement/netting/collateral and returns 0 hits; any-term English search ranks the 2011 interagency CCR 'Legal and Operational Risk Management' section (annual review of netting and collateral agreement enforceability, trading without a master agreement) #1.

S01.label: HQLA haircuts for level 2B assets
S01.why: All-terms plain keyword finds no chunk containing every word and returns 0 hits; Foundry IQ full-text ranks the OCC Liquidity handbook HQLA section stating level 2B assets take a 50% haircut and are capped at 15% of HQLA #1, with two more HQLA sections at #2–3.

S02.label: what happens if a bank runs low on its safety cushion
S02.hint: Running low on the capital buffer
S02.query: what happens if a bank runs low on its safety cushion
S02.why: BM25 matches the words literally and returns the Liquidity 'Fundamentals' chunk, an advanced-approaches parallel-run chunk and a payments safety-and-soundness chunk; vector search maps 'safety cushion' to the FDIC capital conservation buffer sections (#1 and #3), which spell out the payout restrictions.

S02.label: someone pretending to be from my bank talked me into moving my savings
S02.query: someone pretending to be from my bank talked me into moving my savings
S02.why: BM25's top 3 are complaints sharing words like 'bank' and 'savings' (an ACH transfer hold, an account opened without consent, an unemployment-card claim); vector search's top 3 are all fraud-department impersonation scams that pushed consumers to wire their money.

S02.label: how examiners judge whether a bank could survive a sudden loss of funding
S02.query: how examiners judge whether a bank could survive a sudden loss of funding
S02.why: BM25 returns an OFAC examination chunk, payment-system risk text and capital exam procedures (first liquidity hit #4); vector search ranks the OCC Liquidity 'Contingency Funding Plans' section #1.

S02.label: a small lender that wants one simple ratio instead of all the risk weighting math
S02.query: a small lender that wants one simple ratio instead of all the risk weighting math
S02.why: BM25 matches 'risk weighting' literally and returns risk-weight table rows and the FDIC equity risk-weight section; vector search understands 'one simple ratio for a small lender' and ranks the FDIC community bank leverage ratio (CBLR) background #1.

S03.label: wire stuck with an intermediary bank
S03.hint: Wire stuck at an intermediary bank
S03.query: wire stuck with an intermediary bank
S03.why: Keyword-only ranks six FDIC wire-transfer rule chunks (recordkeeping, wire activities, ML risks) that repeat 'wire' and 'intermediary'; vector-only returns other wire complaints (a phone wire, spoofed payment instructions, an account-takeover wire); hybrid's #1/#2 are the complaints where a wire went through an intermediary bank and never arrived or its return could not be traced.

S03.label: ACH transfer failure triggered an account suspension
S03.query: ACH transfer failure triggered an account suspension
S03.why: Keyword-only returns three OCC ACH examination/third-party-sender sections; vector-only's #1 is a complaint about a confirmed wire the bank later rescinded; hybrid fuses both signals and ranks the complaint whose outbound ACH transfer got the account frozen #1.

S03.label: Fedwire reference shows the wire was returned but the sender's account was never credited
S03.query: Fedwire reference shows the wire was returned but the sender's account was never credited
S03.why: Keyword-only latches onto 'Fedwire'/'wire' and returns OCC payment-system credit-risk and Fedwire sections plus FDIC wire guidance; vector-only finds one returned-wire complaint among unrelated wire complaints (1 of 3 relevant); hybrid's top 3 are all returned wires the sender never got credited for (brokerage wire returned but not credited, domestic return discrepancy, fintech with no record of the return).

S04.label: What should a bank do when an incoming wire matches a name on the SDN list?
S04.hint: Incoming wire hits the SDN list
S04.query: What should a bank do when an incoming wire matches a name on the SDN list?
S04.why: The 10 hybrid candidates are all FDIC 8.1 OFAC/wire chunks, but hybrid leads with 'Issuance of OFAC Lists', the 314(a) 'Reporting of Matches' chunk and exam considerations; the semantic reranker promotes 'OFAC Reporting Requirements' (contact OFAC to verify an SDN match, report blocked or rejected items within 10 days) from #5 to #1.

S04.label: Why did the bank ask for my passport when I opened an account as a foreign student?
S04.hint: Passport for a foreign student account
S04.query: Why did the bank ask for my passport when I opened an account as a foreign student?
S04.why: Hybrid ranks seven account-opening complaints first; the semantic reranker lifts the FDIC 8.1 deposit-records section (nonresident aliens must give a passport number) from #9 to #1 and the CIP identifying-information section (passport number and country of issuance for non-U.S. persons) from #8 to #2.

S04.label: What risk weight does a bank assign to a state government's general obligation bonds?
S04.hint: Risk weight for state GO bonds
S04.query: What risk weight does a bank assign to a state government's general obligation bonds?
S04.why: Hybrid leads with the foreign-sovereign risk-weight row, FDIC equity risk weights and past-due risk weights; the semantic reranker recognizes a state as a U.S. public sector entity and promotes the OCC row '20% for general obligations, 50% for revenue obligations' from #4 to #1.

S04.label: What risk weight applies to a loan on an apartment building?
S04.hint: Risk weight for an apartment loan
S04.query: What risk weight applies to a loan on an apartment building?
S04.why: Hybrid ranks the one-to-four-family and presold-builder rows first; the semantic reranker understands 'apartment building' = multifamily and promotes the OCC 'Loans on multifamily properties' row (50% if criteria met, otherwise 100%) from #5 to #1.

S05.label: Zelle scam complaints from Texas
S05.filter: docType eq 'consumer-complaint' and regions/any(r: r eq 'TX')
S05.why: Keyword-only treats 'Texas' as just another word and its #3 is a California Zelle complaint; the region facet filter (regions = TX) plus hybrid ranking returns three Texas complaints about Zelle scams or theft, with category/tag facet counts.

S05.label: international transfer blocked for sanctions screening
S05.query: international transfer blocked for sanctions screening
S05.why: Keyword-only mixes one 2026 complaint with two FDIC OFAC manual chunks; filtering to 2026 consumer complaints returns exactly the three sanctions-blocked international transfer complaints, with the category facet showing where 2026 complaints cluster.

S05.label: wire fraud after an impersonation or email compromise scam
S05.query: wire fraud after an impersonation or email compromise scam
S05.filter: docType eq 'consumer-complaint' and category eq 'Wires and SWIFT' and publishedDate ge 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z
S05.why: Keyword-only's top 3 are 2024/2021 impersonation and wire-fraud complaints plus one 2026 complaint; filtering to 2026 'Wires and SWIFT' complaints returns three current impersonation/business-email-compromise wire frauds.

S05.label: crypto exchange locked my account and won't release my funds
S05.query: crypto exchange locked my account and won't release my funds
S05.filter: docType eq 'consumer-complaint' and category eq 'Virtual currency'
S05.why: Keyword-only's #2 is a non-crypto account restriction complaint (an adult coded as a minor); filtering to the 'Virtual currency' category returns three crypto-platform complaints (an account locked after an income/statement request, a closed brokerage account holding crypto, a blocked stablecoin withdrawal), with a year facet.

S06.label: funds transfer system risks examiners should review for wire transfers
S06.query: funds transfer system risks examiners should review for wire transfers
S06.why: Hybrid's top 5 are all chunks of the superseded March 1990 OCC 'Payment Systems and Funds Transfer Activities' booklet; the freshness profile surfaces the FDIC RMS 8.1 (2026) wire-transfer sections (activities, ML risks, due diligence on wire customers) as #1–3.

S06.label: which banks are required to use the advanced approaches capital rules
S06.hint: Who uses the advanced approaches today
S06.query: which banks are required to use the advanced approaches capital rules
S06.why: Hybrid's top 3 are July 2018 OCC 'Advanced Approaches Banks' chunks that predate the 2019 tailoring rule; the freshness profile ranks the 2026 FDIC tailoring table ('Categories I and II are known as advanced approaches banks') #1 and the Category I (GSIB) row #3.

S06.label: fraudsters impersonating a bank's fraud department to get customers to send money
S06.query: fraudsters impersonating a bank's fraud department to get customers to send money
S06.why: Hybrid's top 3 are consumer scam complaints (a fraud-department impersonator, a spoofed customer-service line, a fraudster's receiving account); the authority profile ranks the OCC Payment Systems 'Fraud Risk Management' section (social engineering, elder abuse, account takeover) #1.

S06.label: instant payment sent to the wrong person and it cannot be pulled back
S06.query: instant payment sent to the wrong person and it cannot be pulled back
S06.why: Hybrid's top 3 are consumer complaints about money sent to the wrong person; the authority profile ranks the OCC Payment Systems 'Real-Time Payments' sections (irrevocable, misdirected payments; payee identification) #1–2.

S07.label: How should a bank handle a wire that matches the SDN list, and what have customers experienced when their transfers were blocked for sanctions?
S07.query: How should a bank handle a wire that matches the SDN list, and what have customers experienced when their transfers were blocked for sanctions?
S07.why: Hybrid's top 3 are all FDIC OFAC/wire guidance; agentic retrieval splits the question and returns OFAC blocking and program guidance at #1–2 plus a consumer's request for a license to release a sanctions-blocked payment at #3.

S07.label: What customer due diligence does the FDIC expect for higher-risk customers, and what do consumers say when their accounts are frozen during KYC reviews?
S07.hint: CDD rules and KYC account freezes
S07.query: What customer due diligence does the FDIC expect for higher-risk customers, and what do consumers say when their accounts are frozen during KYC reviews?
S07.why: Hybrid's top 3 are all FDIC CDD guidance; agentic retrieval interleaves a complaint about a wallet blocked even after KYC documents were submitted (#1), the FDIC higher-risk customer due diligence section (#2) and a complaint about an account limited without explanation whose owner offers KYC documents (#3).

S07.label: What does the OCC expect banks to monitor in ACH activity, and what problems do consumers report when ACH payments are returned or blocked?
S07.query: What does the OCC expect banks to monitor in ACH activity, and what problems do consumers report when ACH payments are returned or blocked?
S07.why: Hybrid's top 3 are all OCC ACH handbook sections; agentic retrieval covers both parts: the ACH mortgage payment returned despite sufficient funds (#1), OCC ACH examination procedures (#2) and a second consumer ACH complaint (blocked ACH pulls or a failed ACH transfer that froze the account, depending on the run) at #3.

S07.label: What fraud risk management does the OCC expect for payment systems, and what do consumers report about impostors posing as their bank's fraud department?
S07.query: What fraud risk management does the OCC expect for payment systems, and what do consumers report about impostors posing as their bank's fraud department?
S07.why: Hybrid's top 3 are all OCC 'Fraud Risk Management' chunks; agentic retrieval returns a fraud-department impersonation complaint (#1), the OCC fraud risk management section (#2) and a second impersonation complaint (#3).

S10.label: PCA thresholds for an adequately capitalized bank
S10.query: PCA thresholds for an adequately capitalized bank
S10.why: Read gives the right page (p. 11) only as flattened page text; Content Understanding layout returns the exact 'Adequately Capitalized' PCA table row (total RBC ≥8%, tier 1 ≥6%, CET1 ≥4.5%, leverage ≥4%) with its page and row.

S10.label: which FDIC rule covers brokered deposits and interest rate restrictions
S10.query: which FDIC rule covers brokered deposits and interest rate restrictions
S10.why: Read returns page 13 as one block of flattened text; Content Understanding layout returns Table 7 row 2 'Brokered Deposits and Interest Rate Restrictions → Sections 337.6 and 337.7 of the FDIC Rules and Regulations' with its page and row.

S10.label: unsettled transactions risk weight
S10.why: Read returns page 89 as flattened text; layout returns Table 13 row 2 'Unsettled transactions' with its 100%/625%/937.5%/1,250% risk weights and page/row coordinates.

S10.label: loans to builders secured by one to four family residential property risk weight
S10.query: loans to builders secured by one to four family residential property risk weight
S10.why: Read returns page 87 as flattened text; layout returns Table 11 row 13 'Loans to builders secured by one- to four-family properties presold under firm contracts' with its 50%/100% risk weight and page/row.

S01.label: AFib DOAC dose when CrCl 15 to 50
S01.query: AFib DOAC dose when CrCl 15 to 50
S01.why: Plain keyword requires every literal term (no stemming, no synonyms) and returns 0 hits; AFTER's synonym map expands AFib to atrial fibrillation and CrCl to creatinine clearance, so its #1 is SAVAYSA 2.1 Nonvalvular Atrial Fibrillation ('Reduce SAVAYSA dose to 30 mg once daily in patients with CrCL 15 to 50 mL/min').

S01.label: latent TB testing before starting a JAK inhibitor
S01.hint: Latent TB screening before JAK inhibitors
S01.query: latent TB testing before starting a JAK inhibitor
S01.why: Plain keyword requires every literal word and returns 0 hits; AFTER's stemming (testing/test) and TB/JAK synonyms put the CIBINQO and LITFULO boxed warnings ('Test for latent TB before and during therapy') in its top 3.

S01.label: SGLT2 DKA risk in T2DM
S01.hint: SGLT2 inhibitors and DKA in T2DM
S01.why: No label chunk contains 'DKA', so the all-terms keyword query returns 0 hits; AFTER expands DKA, T2DM and SGLT2 to the spelled-out terms and ranks JARDIANCE 5.1 Diabetic Ketoacidosis #1.

S01.label: irAE management: systemic corticosteroid dose and taper
S01.query: irAE management: systemic corticosteroid dose and taper
S01.why: No label uses 'irAE', so plain keyword returns 0 hits; the synonym map maps irAE to immune-mediated adverse reactions and AFTER's #1 is LIBTAYO 5.1 ('1 to 2 mg/kg/day prednisone ... taper over at least 1 month').

S02.label: my cholesterol pill makes my muscles ache and my urine looks dark like cola
S02.hint: Statin muscle pain and dark urine
S02.query: my cholesterol pill makes my muscles ache and my urine looks dark like cola
S02.why: BM25 latches onto 'urine'/'dark' in JARDIANCE and LIBTAYO patient-guide text (first statin hit at #7); the vector query ranks the ZOCOR, LIPITOR and pravastatin 'Myopathy and Rhabdomyolysis' warnings #1-#3.

S02.label: weekly diabetes injection and severe belly pain that spreads to the back
S02.query: weekly diabetes injection and severe belly pain that spreads to the back
S02.why: BM25 matches 'weekly'/'injection' to MOUNJARO dosing and LIBTAYO patient text and finds no pancreatitis warning in its top 10; the vector query's #1 is the BYDUREON BCISE 'Acute Pancreatitis' warning.
